# Model configuration   [Skip link to Model configuration](https://docs.leena.ai/docs/model-configuration\#model-configuration)

LLMs are configured at two levels: the **Master Orchestrator (MO)**, which governs the whole bot, and individual **AOPs**, which can either inherit the MO's model or override it. This page covers both, along with the models being retired.

* * *

## Master Orchestrator Model   [Skip link to Master Orchestrator Model](https://docs.leena.ai/docs/model-configuration\#master-orchestrator-model)

Selects the LLM that powers the Master Orchestrator — the model used to interpret user queries, route them, and generate responses. This configuration is also inherited by every AOP on the bot unless an AOP is given its own model.

**Choosing a model:** The picker is organised **provider-first**. Select a provider, then a model. Within each provider, models are listed most capable first, with retiring models at the end. Each model shows a short "best for" line, and newly added models carry a **New** badge.

![](https://files.readme.io/08e5b24ff5dcd5ae177c131884a852162b29e1b6db0aa21c5ae3512c9851baaa-Screenshot_2026-08-24_at_12.01.37_PM.png)

| Provider | Available models |
| --- | --- |
| OpenAI | GPT 6 Astra (New), GPT 6.1 Sol (New), GPT 5.6 Terra (New), GPT 5.5, GPT 4.1 (retiring) |
| Azure OpenAI | GPT 6 Astra (New), GPT 6.1 Sol (New), GPT 5.6 Terra (New), GPT 5.5, GPT 4.1 (retiring) |
| Anthropic | Opus 5.5 (New), Sonnet 5.5 (New), Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.7 (retiring), Opus 4.6 (retiring), Opus 4.5 (retiring) |
| Amazon Bedrock (Anthropic) | Opus 5.5 (New), Sonnet 5.5 (New), Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.7 (retiring), Opus 4.6 (retiring), Opus 4.5 (retiring) |

| Model | Best for |
| --- | --- |
| GPT 6 Astra | Frontier reasoning for the hardest coding and agentic work. |
| GPT 6.1 Sol | Astra-class reasoning for everyday production work at a fraction of its cost. |
| GPT 5.6 Terra | Balanced GPT 5.6 tier for everyday production workloads at lower cost. |
| GPT 5.5 | High throughput for production-scale workloads. |
| GPT 4.1 | Fast and cost-efficient for simple, high-volume tasks. |
| Opus 5.5 | Latest Opus: stronger agentic coding and knowledge work, cheaper than Opus 5. |
| Sonnet 5.5 | Latest Sonnet: capable everyday agent work at Sonnet pricing. |
| Sonnet 4.6 | Balanced speed and quality for everyday tasks. |
| Opus 4.7 | High output for production-scale workloads. |
| Opus 4.6 | Most capable for the most demanding tasks. |
| Opus 4.5 | Strong reasoning for complex tasks at moderate cost. |

The default configuration is **OpenAI — GPT 5.5**. Use the **Compare models** link in the picker header to view benchmarking data before deciding. See [LLM Model Benchmarks](https://docs.leena.ai/docs/model-comparison-benchmarks).

**Model settings:**

- **Effort** — Controls how thoroughly the model thinks before responding (Low / Medium / High). Higher effort improves reasoning quality on complex requests at the cost of response time. Default: Low. Available on every model except GPT 4.1.
- **Priority processing** — Runs requests through a priority lane for faster, more consistent response times. Available on supported models only and **Off by default** where supported:

| Provider | Models with Priority processing |
| --- | --- |
| OpenAI | GPT 6 Astra, GPT 6.1 Sol, GPT 5.6 Terra, GPT 5.5 |
| Azure OpenAI | GPT 5.6 Terra, GPT 5.5 |
| Anthropic | Opus 5.5 |
| Amazon Bedrock (Anthropic) | None |

**How it works:**

- Changes apply on save and take effect from the next user request.
- AOPs inherit this configuration live — changing the model here immediately changes the model every inheriting AOP runs on. AOPs with their own model override are unaffected.
- Run History and the Debugging Console record the resolved provider and model for every run, so you can always trace which model handled a request.

* * *

## AOP Model   [Skip link to AOP Model](https://docs.leena.ai/docs/model-configuration\#aop-model)

Selects the LLM this AOP runs on — the model used to follow the AOP's instructions, make decisions, call tools, and generate responses during execution. Every AOP resolves to a model in one of two ways: inheriting from the Master Orchestrator, or holding its own.

### Inherited from Master Orchestrator (default)   [Skip link to Inherited from Master Orchestrator (default)](https://docs.leena.ai/docs/model-configuration\#inherited-from-master-orchestrator-default)

By default, the AOP uses the Master Orchestrator's model configuration and follows it **live** — if an admin changes the Master Orchestrator's model, every inheriting AOP switches with it, with no action needed on the AOP. The picker shows this at the top as **From orchestrator setting** — _"Uses the model set in Orchestrator settings. Changes there apply here too."_ — so you always know which model the AOP will actually run on.

Inheritance is the right choice for most AOPs: it keeps model management in one place and ensures consistent behaviour across the bot.

![](https://files.readme.io/53db3df69e182431543520b7957b8d8b00fdf419391a6539e9a440796d5c57b0-Screenshot_2026-08-24_at_12.02.35_PM.png)

### Or choose a specific model (override)   [Skip link to Or choose a specific model (override)](https://docs.leena.ai/docs/model-configuration\#or-choose-a-specific-model-override)

Override the inherited model when this AOP has different cost, speed, or reasoning needs than the rest of the bot — for example, a simple acknowledgement AOP that doesn't need a heavyweight model, or a complex multi-step decision flow that benefits from deeper reasoning.

The picker is organised **provider-first**. Select a provider, then a model:

| Provider | Available models |
| --- | --- |
| OpenAI | GPT 6 Astra (New), GPT 6.1 Sol (New), GPT 5.6 Terra (New), GPT 5.5, GPT 4.1 (retiring) |
| Azure OpenAI | GPT 6 Astra (New), GPT 6.1 Sol (New), GPT 5.6 Terra (New), GPT 5.5, GPT 4.1 (retiring) |
| Anthropic | Opus 5.5 (New), Sonnet 5.5 (New), Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.7 (retiring), Opus 4.6 (retiring), Opus 4.5 (retiring) |
| Amazon Bedrock (Anthropic) | Opus 5.5 (New), Sonnet 5.5 (New), Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.7 (retiring), Opus 4.6 (retiring), Opus 4.5 (retiring) |

An overriding AOP stores its own full configuration (provider, model, and model settings) and is **unaffected by Master Orchestrator changes**. Re-selecting **From orchestrator setting** at the top of the picker returns the AOP to live inheritance.

Use the **Compare models** link in the picker header to view benchmarking data before deciding.

**Model settings:**

- **Effort** — Controls how thoroughly the model thinks before responding (Low / Medium / High). Higher effort improves reasoning quality on complex, multi-step AOPs at the cost of response time. Default: Low.
- **Priority processing** — Runs requests through a priority lane for faster, more consistent response times. Available on supported models only (see the table above) and **Off by default** where supported.

**How it works:**

- Changes apply on save and take effect from the AOP's **next run** — in-flight runs are not affected.
- The AOP details page shows the effective model, e.g. "GPT 5.5 · OpenAI · High · Priority".
- Run History and the Debugging Console record the resolved provider and model for every run (marked as inherited where applicable), so you can always trace which model handled a request.
- Existing AOPs default to inheriting the Master Orchestrator's configuration; nothing changes until you explicitly override.

* * *

## Retiring models   [Skip link to Retiring models](https://docs.leena.ai/docs/model-configuration\#retiring-models)

Models being phased out stay in the picker with an **"Available until 30 November 2026"** badge. Hover over the badge to see the replacement, e.g. _"We're removing this model on 30 November 2026. Opus 5.5 will be selected automatically. Switch earlier if you'd prefer a different model."_

| Retiring model | Providers | Available until | Automatically moves to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GPT 4.1 | OpenAI, Azure OpenAI | 30 November 2026 | GPT 5.6 Terra |
| Opus 4.5 | Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock | 30 November 2026 | Opus 5.5 |
| Opus 4.6 | Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock | 30 November 2026 | Opus 5.5 |
| Opus 4.7 | Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock | 30 November 2026 | Opus 5.5 |
| Sonnet 4.6 | Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock | 30 November 2026 | Sonnet 5.5 |

**What happens on the retirement date:**

- Nothing breaks. Any Master Orchestrator or AOP still set to a retiring model automatically runs on its replacement — no action needed.
- Retired models remain visible in the picker but are greyed out and can't be selected.
- To choose a different model than the automatic replacement, switch before the retirement date.
